30.text: The relations between the Reindeer and the Maritime Chukchee are more

31.text: complicated, since the breeders, though rich in reindeer, depend on the Mari-

32.text: time hunters for thongs, seal-skins, and especially for blubber and walrus-meat,

33.text: which, as I said before, are considered the most palatable of the common diet.

34.text: Moreover, the Maritime hunter is more daring, used to greater danger and to

35.text: every kind of adventure, than the lonely herdsman living on the dull plain,

36.text: always encumbered with his herd. However, a herdsman is considered to be

37.text: much more amply equipped for life; and every year young men and whole

38.text: families go from various Maritime villages to the Reindeer camps, often far

39.text: inland. They settle as “dwelling-mates,” marry into families of the Reindeer

40.text: people, and gradually acquire a competency of their own. The Eskimo of

41.text: the Pacific shore, some forty years ago, were, on the contrary, in a position
